# Launch Notes

The launch plan assumes a small, curated document set bundled directly with the application deployment.

Version one will run on Vercel using a server-side Node.js route for question answering. The bundled retrieval index is generated before deployment and shipped with the app.

Because the runtime is serverless, the deployment should not depend on rebuilding embeddings during request handling. If the Gemini API key is missing during build time, the app can still render the document list, but question answering stays disabled until the index is regenerated.

PDF files must be text-readable in version one. Scanned PDFs are not supported.

Docwise AI is a small internal question-and-answer tool for a preloaded document library.

The app should answer only from the documents that ship with the deployment bundle. If the library does not support the question, the app must refuse instead of improvising.

The first release is single-turn only. Users ask one question at a time and review the answer alongside the supporting evidence.

Answers should stay concise by default. The system can mention when multiple documents appear to conflict, but it should not collapse those disagreements into a single invented conclusion.

chunks.text:
# Support Playbook

The support team targets a first response within one business day for standard internal requests.

High-severity launch blockers should be escalated to the operations lead within two hours of confirmation. If the blocker affects billing or contract obligations, the finance partner must also be notified the same day.

When a customer question falls outside the product documentation, the support team should admit that the current library is incomplete and route the issue to product operations instead of guessing.

Support notes should include the original question, the linked document sources, and the final response that was sent back to the requester.
